findings.title: Feature-flagged table widgets render an empty table instead of query results
findings.body: When `organization.features.includes('use-table-widget-visualization')` is true, this branch renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with `columns={[]}` and a hard-coded empty `tableData` instead of using the available `fields`, `result.meta`, and `result.data`. Real query results are ignored, so any organization with this flag enabled would see blank table dashboard widgets. Either wire the real result into `TableWidgetVisualization` or remove this branch before enabling the flag.

findings.title: Replay error timestamps and breadcrumb timestamps use incompatible units
findings.body: `error_events` are populated from nodestore event data where `timestamp` is the absolute event timestamp, while replay segment breadcrumb `timestamp` values are relative seconds from the replay start. `gen_request_data` compares these directly with `error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0)`, so real requests will interleave errors at the wrong position in the generated log stream, likely grouping all errors at the beginning or end. The unit test uses small values for both and therefore does not catch the unit mismatch. Normalize error timestamps to replay-relative time before merging.

findings.title: User-controlled issue title is embedded unescaped in a Markdown link
findings.body: `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` formats `MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE`, which wraps the raw issue title inside a Markdown link label: `[**{title}**]({url})`. `_truncate_title` only truncates and does not escape characters such as `]`, `(`, backticks, or newlines. An issue title from event data can break out of the link or inject Markdown into the bot's PR/merge-request comment. Sanitize or escape the title before placing it inside the link label.

findings.title: Zero value for `age` or `timestamp` bypasses mutual-exclusion validation
findings.body: The mutual-exclusion checks use truthiness: `validate_timestamp` does `if self.initial_data.get("age")`, and `validate_age` does the equivalent for `timestamp`. Since `0` is falsy, a report containing both `timestamp` and `age: 0` (or `timestamp: 0` and an age) passes both validators even though the two spec variants are supposed to be mutually exclusive. Use an explicit presence check such as `if "age" in self.initial_data` and add tests for zero values.
